title: Brent nears $89 as US vows 'unprecedented' Iran measures, blockade holds
content: Brent crude rose more than 5% this week to settle around $88.91/bbl by 14 August 2026. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington would unveil economic measures against Iran "never seen" in the history of sanctions, layered atop an ongoing US naval blockade of Iranian ports that Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said could run indefinitely; officials estimate the blockade has already cost Tehran roughly $4.8bn in lost oil revenue. Iran said the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until sanctions are eased and frozen funds released. The IEA warned of the widest global oil supply deficit in five years. The escalation is stoking inflation risks already cited by the ECB, which raised rates in June partly on Middle East-driven price pressure.

title: US CPI cools to 3.4% in July, S&P 500 hits record above 7,800
content: US headline CPI rose 0.1% m/m in July, data released 12 August showed, with the annual rate easing to 3.4% from 3.5%; core CPI rose 0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y, with gasoline prices down 2.9%. The cooler-than-expected print eased fears that the July jobs shock signalled a wider inflation problem, trimming September Fed hike bets to around 48% from roughly 58% before the report. The S&P 500 rose 0.65% to a record closing high of 7,798.99, its 27th record close of the year, while gold climbed 1.2% to around $4,424/oz and the dollar weakened. UST yields fell as traders judged the data left the Fed room to hold rates steady next month.

title: US retail sales fall 0.6% in July, stocks slip from record but post 3rd weekly gain
content: US retail sales fell 0.6% m/m in July, Census Bureau data released 14 August showed, well below forecasts of a modest 0.1-0.2% rise; autos led the decline, down 1.8%, with non-store (online) sales off 2.2%. Annual growth slowed sharply to 5.0% from 7.3% in May. A preliminary University of Michigan survey also showed consumer sentiment deteriorating in August as inflation concerns lingered. The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% on the day, having set a fresh record close of 7,798.99 on 12 August, but still notched a third straight weekly gain, its longest winning run since May; the Russell 2000 hit a fresh record. The data added to signs of a cooling but still resilient US consumer.
